title: Optoelectronic devices
blurb: Explain photoconductors, photovoltaic cells, optoisolators, solid-state relays and optical shaft encoders.

E6F01.why: Photons carry the light's energy and **electrons absorb it**, freeing them to make current.
E6F01.trap: Photons deliver the energy; they are not what absorbs it.

E6F02.why: Light frees carriers in photoconductive material, so its **resistance decreases**.
E6F02.trap: Reflectivity is not what changes; resistance is.

E6F03.why: The usual optoisolator is an **LED shining on a phototransistor**, in one package.
E6F03.trap: Lasers and photomultipliers are not used in optocouplers.

E6F04.why: The photovoltaic effect is **light converted to electrical energy**, as in a solar cell.
E6F04.trap: Light emission when voltage is applied is the LED effect, the reverse.

E6F05.why: An optical shaft encoder detects rotation when a **patterned wheel interrupts a light beam**.
E6F05.trap: It senses rotation, not light strength, and generates no RTTY.

E6F06.why: Photoconductive devices are most commonly made from a **crystalline semiconductor**.
E6F06.trap: Argon and polyphenol acetate are not photoconductive materials.

E6F07.why: A solid-state relay **uses semiconductors to perform the functions of an electromechanical relay**.
E6F07.trap: Transistors driving a coil still leave a mechanical relay.

E6F08.why: Optoisolators provide **electrical isolation** between the control circuit and the circuit being switched.
E6F08.trap: Isolation means no electrical link, not a low-impedance link.

E6F09.why: Efficiency is the **fraction of the light converted** to electrical output.
E6F09.trap: Voltage divided by current is a resistance-like ratio, not efficiency.

E6F10.why: Power-generating solar cells are made of **silicon**.
E6F10.trap: Silicon, not selenium or cadmium sulfide, is the common power-cell material.

E6F11.why: A fully lit silicon cell produces about **0.5 V** open-circuit.
E6F11.trap: 0.7 V is a conducting diode's drop, a different thing.
